title: Valid Sudoku
keyIdea: Check the filled cells once: each digit must be new in its row, its column and its 3×3 box. Keep 27 sets (9 rows, 9 columns, 9 boxes); box index = (i / 3) * 3 + j / 3.

approaches.name: Three passes: rows, columns, boxes
approaches.idea: For each i, check row i, column i and box i with fresh 9-slot counters.
approaches.why: Each cell is read three times; only 9-slot arrays at a time.

approaches.name: One pass with 27 sets
approaches.idea: For every filled cell: if its digit is already in rows[i], cols[j] or boxes[box] → false; otherwise insert into all three.
approaches.why: 81 cells, O(1) set operations each. The board is always 9×9, so it's constant either way.

quiz.q: Must the board be solvable to be valid?
options: No: only the filled cells are checked against the three rules

quiz.q: Why check all three sets before inserting?
options: A repeat in any of row, column or box makes the board invalid
